parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime shows no documented traveller-facing exposure: same-sex conduct decriminalised (2016), no trans-specific criminal or expression statute, no documented police targeting, no documented violence incidents, and a 2014 immigration-detention rule barring discrimination on gender identity — directly relevant if a visitor enters that facility. Documented positives include SOGI-rights diplomatic positions. Offsetting gaps: no legal recognition, no general anti-discrimination protection, no prison-placement data, no documented border or document practice, thin enforcement evidence, and a low composite index (not trans-specific). Extrapolating from decriminalisation plus functioning treaty reporting without any criminalisation signal lands mid-Reduced Risk, with genuine uncertainty rather than documented danger.

entry_documents.exposure: No documented border, passport-marker or document-mismatch friction for trans visitors.
entry_documents.protection: No documented entry restriction; 2016 decriminalisation removes criminal exposure at inspection.
entry_documents.interaction: Unknown how document presentation is handled at entry; absence of record is not evidence of smooth practice.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented arrests, detentions or custody incidents involving trans people; corrections placement by birth sex undocumented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Immigration-detention facility rules (2014) prohibit discrimination on sex/gender, sexual preference or gender identity.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: That protection covers immigration detention only, not criminal-justice prisons; enforcement practice of the rules is unsourced.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No geographic subnational variation documented; institutional divide between immigration detention (protected) and prisons (no data).
federal_state_facilities.protection: Island-wide 2016 repeal; facility-level non-discrimination inside the processing centre.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor entering the criminal-justice system would face an unprotected, undocumented regime.

care_services.exposure: No documented emergency-care denial or medication seizure for trans visitors.
care_services.interaction: No record either way on HRT continuity or insurance treatment for visitors.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No trans-specific criminal offence, morality provision or documented police extortion/arrest practice.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Country signed the 2011 joint statement on ending SOGI-based violence; decriminalisation reaffirmed in 2016.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Low composite equality index is a climate signal, not a documented traveller-facing enforcement record.

minors_guardians.exposure: No documented rules, incidents or custody/facility treatment specific to trans travellers with minors.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family's exposure rests on the same undocumented entry and care pathways as solo adults.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No dated incidents, rates or patterns of anti-trans violence recorded; no evidence either direction in this thin record.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No documented state-tolerated violence; diplomatic support for SOGI rights.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Zero documented incidents in a thin dossier cannot be read as proof of safety.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No general non-discrimination statute for visitors; no trans-recognition route; enforcement of detention rules unsourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Detention rules provide a formal non-discrimination basis; functioning UN treaty reporting suggests institutional capacity.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedy pathway outside the processing centre is entirely undocumented.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra bars entry via a universal Visitor Conduct Register. This dossier documents no entry bar, registration, screening referral or any universal-exposure measure against trans visitors — materially safer than 0.35-A, whose defining feature is absent here.

Kestrel Isles documents routine secondary screening, discretionary refusal and slow appeals for trans visitors. Here no such border friction is recorded at all; the comparison is a documented administrative exposure versus an undocumented (not disproven) one, so this rates somewhat above 0.55-B.

Meridia documents trained border staff, a working tribunal, counsel access and compensation. This dossier has one narrow detention non-discrimination rule and no demonstrated remedies for visitors — far less documented protection, so it sits clearly below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The regime's documented profile is decriminalisation plus symbolic SOGI diplomacy, with a single traveller-relevant protection inside immigration detention. Every heavy exposure tier — universal document/facility exclusion, state-directed targeting, hostility with no recourse — is simply undocumented rather than absent. Resident-facing gaps (no recognition, no employment protection, no treaty-body account) are climate signals only under Rule 1 and do not drive the score downward as visitor exposure. The low composite index is not trans-specific and carries little weight. Thin data caps the rating: structural signals (no criminalisation, no targeting record, functioning state machinery) extrapolate to moderate safety, while unverified border, care and prison-placement practices prevent a Reduced-Risk-plus placement.
